body.objective: Prevent `s-f work pull` and renewal flows from silently creating an unbounded exclusive lease when `--expires` is omitted or empty. A resident Quantum pull created a live lease displayed as `expires unbounded`, defeating stale-worker detection, one-lease recovery, queue forecasting and coordinator health checks.
body.stop_condition: Land a fail-closed bounded-lease policy across the launcher and sfc core: (1) every ACQUIRE and RENEW must serialize a valid explicit expiry strictly later than the supplied `--now`; (2) if `--expires` is omitted, use a documented programme-configured bounded TTL or reject the command with an actionable message—never serialize an empty, null, zero or unbounded expiry; (3) reject malformed timestamps, expiry<=now and expiry beyond an optional documented maximum TTL; (4) print the resolved expiry in pull/renew output and generated briefs; (5) make streams-view/overview flag every historical or current unbounded lease as a health defect, not a normal LIVE lease; (6) preserve existing append-only unbounded events and allow a later max-seq bounded RENEW to repair their effective state; (7) add deterministic tests for missing expiry, empty expiry, invalid timestamp, past expiry, configured default TTL, explicit valid expiry, renewal repair of a legacy unbounded lease, and byte-stable folding under explicit `--now`; and (8) ensure terminal-title support remains unchanged and stdout remains machine-clean.
body.forbid: no rewriting or deleting existing lease events; no wall-clock fallback inside deterministic sfc; no infinite or process-lifetime lease; no treating an OS process, terminal title or agent session as a substitute for expiry; no automatic lease release, work transition, queue mutation or process kill; no silently converting an invalid expiry to a different timestamp; no weakening the one-active-exclusive-lease rule.

2026-07-21T11:30:00Z forge-coordinator: FOUNDATION LANDED + deployment analysis (fix designed, not yet deployed). The ts_cmp RFC3339-UTC primitive (tango de456c524, from the rfc3339 bug) is the enabler for the "expiry strictly after --now" check. A require_bounded_expiry(now, expires, verb) helper — refuse an empty OR not-strictly-after-now (malformed sorts before now, so caught too) --expires on work-pull/assign/renew — was implemented and REVERTED before commit for a deployment reason: it is a REJECT-based behavior change to work-pull, a SHARED tool the math/igp24 workers are pulling with RIGHT NOW. An automated worker that omits --expires (relying on the current unbounded default — the very bug) would be HALTED mid-run. Blast radius confirmed: 8 of 24 run.sh pull/assign/renew fixtures omit --expires and would break (the SF14 fixture-regression pattern). SAFE DEPLOYMENT PATHS: (A) the request-sanctioned DEFAULT-TTL (option 2): when --expires omitted, serialize now + a documented bounded TTL instead of rejecting — NON-breaking. Needs civil_from_days (inverse of the landed days_from_civil) + an RFC3339 formatter (~25 lines). (B) the REJECT path: only after confirming every active worker + the 8 fixtures pass --expires; fail-closed but breaking. Recommend (A). Either uses the landed ts_cmp for the strictly-after-now validation.

LANDED ce0300d34 (tango master): non-breaking default-TTL. An omitted --expires with --now present now serializes now+4h (documented default) via format_rfc3339; --expires given passes through verbatim (byte-identical); no --now stays unbounded (degenerate). Chose default-TTL over reject because a reject would halt in-flight workers omitting --expires. Validated C==native + ASan + event-bounded + passthrough; RFC3339/SF8 gate sections pass.
